name: Anton Shah
life: “I still remember a child's shadow puppet shaped like a leaf.” Thursday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Anton pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I used the leaves to teach shadows to a child in isolation. She still draws the missing leaf.
appearance: Anton is easy to recognize by short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat and a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Usually dressed in a boxy denim jacket with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket, Anton starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak when listening.
personality: Anton loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Anton remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To give the isolated pupil a new leaf shadow.
family: Pat Fraser is Anton’s cousin. Anton calls about good news first. Pat is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The free fringe*, Pat says, “I heard their conversation through the wall and realized I owed my old shop partner a call.”
connections: Jay Knight. A patient remembered by the smell of leaves becomes part of the child's shadow lesson.
